500._measured: 2026-10-19 on darwin/arm64, Apple M3 Max (14 cores), n=500 schemas in one generated gen package, s=100 services, three runs after relations stopped naming their target's metadata in the Desc (the use site names it). 1-minute load average before each run: 2.57, 6.00, 11.37 (only the first was under 4: the machine was busy with other work for the 30 minutes the harness waited, so runs 2 and 3 are recorded at that load and the times are, if anything, high). Cold build 23.7, 22.7, 25.3 s; schema edit + regenerate + rebuild 20.2, 20.6, 22.4 s; service binary 5.66 MB in all three (and at n=100); link peak 278.6, 273.7, 279.3 MB. The largest of each: cold 25.27 s, schema edit 22.44 s, service 5.66 MB, link 279.3 MB. Times are 4x the largest (CI runners have fewer, slower cores; recalibrate from the first GitHub run). Sizes and memory are 1.5x, not the 2x of the old rule: the binary was identical across the three runs and across loads, and the link peak varied by 2%, so neither depends on the machine's load, and a tighter margin keeps the thresholds meaningful. At 11.33 MB (2x) a leak of a few hundred entities back into a service would pass, and at 558 MB the link peak of the earlier connected-graph build (404 MB, 23.6 MB binary) would pass; these thresholds fail it

500-graphql._measured: 2026-10-22 on darwin/arm64, Apple M3 Max (14 cores), the -graphql variant: n=500 schemas that also carry velox-graphql's annotations (a root query field, OrderField and WhereOps on name), generated with -plugin velox-graphql into one gen package, s=100 services that each call the root connection function and the next edge's method of five entities. Three runs started at 1-minute load averages of 3.19, 3.87 and 3.11 (under 4; the load rose to 10 to 25 during runs 2 and 3, the machine being shared). Cold build 78.8, 74.9, 81.5 s; schema edit + regenerate + rebuild 75.9, 76.0, 77.4 s; service binary 11.11 MB in all three (and 11.1 MB at n=20, so it is flat in n); link peak 636.6, 662.2, 625.7 MB. The largest of each: cold 81.51 s, schema edit 77.40 s, service 11.11 MB, link 662.2 MB. Two earlier runs, run at once at load averages of 70 to 80, took 474 and 510 s cold and 396 and 351 s for the edit (and 633.9 and 636.3 MB, 11.11 MB): they say the times follow the machine's load, and are not used. Thresholds by the rule of the 500 entry: times 4x the largest, sizes and memory 1.5x. The service is twice the plain variant's 5.66 MB because it links the GraphQL runtime, which does not grow with n. A later -check run at load averages of 10 to 34 measured cold 171.9 s and schema edit 461.7 s, over the edit threshold: under that load the time thresholds fail, as the runs at load 70 did. Recalibrate the times from the first Linux CI run, and re-measure on an idle machine (followups, 1.0 release)
